intended_object: A projection on bit strings that takes the first component (the unary row index) out of an encoded matrix-entry request. It is used inside the library's polynomial-time machine encoding. This is inferred from the docstring and from `machinePairFirst`.
explanation: The definition is just `machinePairFirst word`, which unfolds to `Cobham.fstBlock word`: it takes the first block of a paired bit-string code. Its only job is to name, for this library's own encoding of matrix-entry requests, the field that carries the row index. Choices like this are made to fit the library's complexity-theory proofs (here, showing that functions lie in FP). The literature does not define a matching object, so this is an auxiliary encoding helper rather than a mathematical object.
